newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Budget boosts Irish govt ratings, early poll seen.
newsitem.headline: Budget boosts Irish govt ratings, early poll seen.

text.p: The biggest budget tax cuts in Irish history have boosted the popularity of Prime Minister John Bruton's coalition government and increased the likelihood of an early election, the Irish Times said on Saturday.
It published an opinion poll showing that the satisfaction rating of the government had increased to the highest level since it came to office in November 1994 when the previous coalition collapsed.

The survey said the rating was up 11 percent from 39 percent six weeks ago to 50 percent following last month's budget in which the standard rate of income tax was cut for the first time in five years.
Bruton's own personal rating was up five points to 58 percent, the survey said.
An election must be held by November this year but most analysts believe Bruton will capitalise on the warm reception for his tax cuts and call an early poll in May or June.
The government says it has the fastest-growing economy in the European Union and is making major inroads into a stubbornly high 11 percent jobless rate.
